news.title: WashU admissions strategy is working — and evolving
news.summary_en: WashU boosted admissions outreach, enrolled 1,942 students in the Class of 2030 and is adding early action for the 2031 class. Leaders highlight strong international interest, growing student focus on AI and career outcomes and an upcoming review of the university’s test-optional policy.

news.title: Rediscovering Grete Stern and Horacio Coppola
news.summary_en: Horacio Coppola and Grete Stern are pivotal figures in the art of 20th century Argentina. Beginning Sept. 9, the WashU Kemper Art Museum will explore their legacy as part of “Buenos Aires Modern, 1935–1950,” the first U.S. exhibition to examine how local, exile and immigrant artists adopted and transformed the aesthetics of international modernism.

news.title: Some assembly required, with machine learning
news.summary_en: WashU researchers are working on ways to use machine learning to not just make predictions about potential chemical compounds but also to model out the synthesis of those materials.

news.title: Sam Fox School fall Public Lecture Series begins Aug. 31
news.summary_en: More than a dozen nationally and internationally known artists, architects, designers and scholars will discuss their work as part of the Sam Fox School’s fall Public Lecture Series.

news.title: The Longest Table returns to WashU
news.summary_en: A WashU tradition, the Longest Table invites students to build connections, enjoy a meal and engage in meaningful conversations about the community and civic issues that matter to them most.

news.title: WashU astronomers selected for Roman space telescope programs
news.summary_en: Scheduled to launch Aug. 30, scientists will use Roman to settle essential questions in the areas of dark energy, exoplanets and astrophysics. WashU plays a key role in four new projects.

news.title: How to navigate conflicting childhood vaccine guidance
news.summary_en: Jennifer Layden of Bursky Public Health explains conflicting childhood vaccine guidance, drawing on her experience leading state outbreak responses and national vaccination efforts at the CDC.

news.title: ‘Buy now, pay later’ may reshape retail prices, inventory, WashU research finds
news.summary_en: New research from WashU Olin Business finds popular installment payment plans are changing not only how consumers pay, but also the prices they face and the way retailers manage their businesses.

news.title: A painless punch with a microneedle patch could detect kidney disease earlier
news.summary_en: New research from the lab of WashU McKelvey Engineering’s Srikanth Singamaneni shows the early success of a microneedle patch that can be applied on the skin to capture biomarkers of kidney injury. It may one day support home or point-of-care monitoring.
